title: Will mpox go global again? Research shows it's evolving in curious ways - Nature
snippet: Analyses of mpox clades currently in circulation provide clues to how the virus managed to spread worldwide in 2022 — and how it might go global again. As mpox continues to spark localized outbreaks in Africa and, on occasion, in other parts of the world, researchers are racing to understand how the virus managed to spread globally in 2022 — and how it might do so again. Clade Ia: this clade has been spreading in Central Africa since the virus was first discovered to infect humans in 1970. In 2025, there was a large increase in infections with clade I mpox, which historically caused sporadic but deadly outbreaks in rural parts of Central Africa. Over the past couple of years, researchers have been racing to understand how the new mpox clades, Ib and IIb, differ from their predecessors. Rats infected with clade Ib mpox had higher survival rates than those infected with clade Ia, yet they transmitted just as much infectious virus.

title: Children make up half of mpox cases in Guinea-Bissau as epidemic spreads - The Guardian
snippet: # Children make up half of mpox cases in Guinea-Bissau as epidemic spreads. More than half of the mpox cases reported in Guinea-Bissau have been among children, local authorities have said, almost two months since the country announced an epidemic. A national outbreak was declared on 4 July, just over a week after a 27-year-old woman became the first confirmed case of mpox in the west African country. Since then, there have been seven confirmed cases and 46 suspected cases. In a statement on Thursday, Unicef warned that because the country’s health surveillance systems were fragile, the virus is probably spreading undetected, leaving even more children at risk. Sandra Martins, the country’s deputy representative for Unicef, said: “This is the first time mpox cases have been reported in Guinea-Bissau, making even a small outbreak a major public health event.”. In Guinea-Bissau, that is no different but there is also a sense of urgency, with primary schools scheduled to reopen across the country in September.

title: Colorado sees summer surge in Mpox infections - Denver7
snippet: DENVER — Colorado is nearing last year's total number of Mpox cases after health officials reported a recent uptick in infections, including seven cases since late July. Colorado is nearing last year's total number of Mpox cases after health officials reported a recent uptick in infections, including seven cases since late July. The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has recorded 18 cases this year, compared with 21 reported statewide in all of 2025. In Denver alone, the Denver Department of Public Health and Environment (DDPHE) has seen six cases since June 1. “The recent Denver cases have no known connections or common exposures, although cases can cluster in time,” Denver Department of Public Health and Environment public information officer Ryann Money said. title: San Francisco reports first case of more severe mpox strain - San Francisco Chronicle
snippet: San Francisco public health officials on Wednesday confirmed the city’s first case of clade I mpox, a strain of the virus that officials say may cause more severe illness than the type behind the outbreak in 2022. While clade I mpox cases remain rare in the United States, clade II mpox cases continue to occur in San Francisco and throughout California,” Dr. Susan Philip, the city’s health officer, said in a statement. The announcement puts San Francisco on a short list of U.S. jurisdictions to report clade I infections, which federal officials have been tracking as outbreaks continue in parts of Africa and occasional cases surface in the United States and Europe. But federal health officials have also said they are still monitoring cases to better understand how severe clade I infections are in the United States, where reported cases remain rare. San Francisco officials said the vaccine offers protection against both clade I and clade II.
